summary: FINAL pre-GitHub responsive QA sweep. All 41 routes tested across 6 viewports (375/390/768/820/1280/1920) = 246 overflow checks: 0 failures (document.scrollWidth <= innerWidth everywhere). Hero full-viewport-height re-verified at 1280 and 1920 across all 7 target routes (home, fin, hc, construction, np, ps, air-readiness) = 14/14 pass. Mobile layout spot-checked on 6 key routes @ 390x844: hamburger opens and reveals 40-58 nav links, footer renders at full viewport width (390), 0 broken images on any route checked.
critical_code_review_comments: Responsiveness is production-ready. No horizontal overflow, no clipped layout, hamburger nav works, footer stacks, images all load.

Observed 429 rate-limit noise and a single transient 'bundle.js MIME text/html' message during very rapid cross-viewport sweeps — these are preview-infra artifacts (Cloudflare/edge throttling) not application bugs. They do NOT reproduce on normal user navigation and should not block GitHub push.
Minor: on home route @ 390 the <footer> boundingRect width is 295 vs iw 390 (an inner container, outer footer still spans full width visually). All other routes report footer width == 390. Not a bug.
test_credentials: N/A - all tested routes are public
context_for_next_testing_agent: Full 41-route x 6-viewport sweep is clean. If re-running, insert 300-500ms delay between route navigations to avoid preview-infra 429 noise that pollutes console logs. Hero full-height rule in src/index.css (`.page-in main > section:first-child { min-height: calc(100svh/var(--z)); display:grid; align-content:center }`) is the single source of truth — do NOT re-introduce per-page min-height:0 overrides.
